section: India and the WTO - agreements, ministerial conferences, public stockholding, fisheries subsidies, appellate body crisis
subsections: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access
WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment

accepted.s: The Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) rests on which of the following three pillars?
o: Domestic support, market access and export competition
Market access, investment protection and government procurement
Export competition, services and industrial subsidies
Domestic support, intellectual property and trade facilitation
accepted.x: The AoA has three pillars: domestic support, market access and export competition.
accepted.tq: Identify the standard three-part structure of the agreement.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Blue Box support under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Research expenditure with no production connection
Direct payments linked to unlimited expansion of production
Direct payments under production-limiting programmes
All subsidies prohibited under the SCM Agreement
accepted.x: Blue Box support consists of direct payments connected with production-limiting programmes. Although trade-distorting, such support is exempt from reduction commitments.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the production-limiting feature of the Blue Box from Green and Amber categories.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to Amber Box subsidies, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are direct payments that limit production and are exempt from all reductions.
They include price- or quantity-linked support such as MSP and input subsidies, measured through AMS.
They are support measures unrelated to prices or quantities and therefore have no limits.
They refer only to export subsidies paid to least developed countries.
accepted.x: Amber Box support covers price- or quantity-linked measures, including MSP, power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation subsidies. Such support is trade-distorting and is measured as Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS).
accepted.tq: Use the examples of price and input support to identify the Amber Box.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an official subsidy box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Green Box
Amber Box
Red Box
Blue Box
accepted.x: Green, Blue and Amber are the subsidy boxes under the AoA. Red, Orange and Yellow are not AoA boxes; a prohibited-subsidy category described as a red-light category belongs to the SCM context.
accepted.tq: Find the odd term in a closely related list of official categories.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support is generally what percentage of the value of agricultural output for developing countries?
o: 5 per cent
10 per cent
15 per cent
20 per cent
accepted.x: Developing countries are allowed Amber support up to 10 per cent of the value of agricultural output under the de minimis provision.
accepted.tq: Recall the country-category distinction in a percentage-based provision.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support applicable to developed countries is:
o: 15 per cent of agricultural output
10 per cent of agricultural output
2 per cent of agricultural output
5 per cent of agricultural output
accepted.x: For developed countries, Amber support within 5 per cent of the value of agricultural output is allowed without penalty under the de minimis provision.
accepted.tq: Compare the two country-specific thresholds rather than reversing them.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the market-access commitments of the Agreement on Agriculture, developed countries were required to reduce tariffs by 36 per cent over six years, whereas developing countries were required to reduce them by:
o: 36 per cent over ten years
12 per cent over five years
24 per cent over ten years
30 per cent over eight years
accepted.x: The specified commitment for developing countries was a 24 per cent tariff reduction over ten years, compared with 36 per cent over six years for developed countries.
accepted.tq: Match both the percentage and time period instead of relying on one figure alone.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The conversion of non-tariff agricultural barriers into tariffs under the Agreement on Agriculture is known as:
o: Countervailing
Tariffication
Harmonisation
Graduation
accepted.x: Tariffication means converting non-tariff barriers into tariff equivalents as part of the market-access commitments.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact technical term for a policy process.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The highest decision-making body of the World Trade Organization is required to meet:
o: Only when requested by the Director-General
At least once every two years
Every year without exception
Once in five years
accepted.x: The WTO Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body and meets at least once every two years under the Marrakesh Agreement.
accepted.tq: Recall the institutional hierarchy and minimum meeting frequency.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding WTO Ministerial Conferences:

List-I (Conference)
a. First Ministerial Conference
b. Second Ministerial Conference
c. Third Ministerial Conference
d. Fourth Ministerial Conference

List-II (Venue and year)
i. Seattle, 1999
ii. Singapore, 1996
iii. Doha, 2001
iv. Geneva, 1998

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii
a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i
a–ii, b–i, c–iv, d–iii
a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii
accepted.x: MC1 was held at Singapore in 1996, MC2 at Geneva in 1998, MC3 at Seattle in 1999 and MC4 at Doha in 2001.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure venue-year pair and eliminate codes.

accepted.s: Which of the following was associated with the First WTO Ministerial Conference held at Singapore in 1996?
o: The adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The Singapore issues and the Information Technology Agreement
The beginning of the e-commerce customs-duty moratorium
accepted.x: The Singapore Ministerial Conference introduced the Singapore issues—investment, competition, procurement transparency and trade facilitation—and was associated with the Information Technology Agreement.
accepted.tq: Link a conference with its distinctive outcome rather than its venue alone.

accepted.s: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was begun at which WTO Ministerial Conference?
o: MC9, Bali, 2013
MC1, Singapore, 1996
MC2, Geneva, 1998
MC4, Doha, 2001
accepted.x: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium began at the Second Ministerial Conference in Geneva in 1998.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between successive early Ministerial Conferences using their outcomes.

accepted.s: The Third WTO Ministerial Conference at Seattle in 1999 is remembered chiefly because it:
o: Collapsed amid protests
Adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement
Ended agricultural export subsidies
Adopted the Bali Package
accepted.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 collapsed amid protests.
accepted.tq: Associate a highly distinctive event with the correct conference.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Fourth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Doha in 2001?
o: The Bali Package and interim Peace Clause were adopted.
The e-commerce moratorium was begun and the Singapore issues were introduced.
The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched and a TRIPS-public health declaration was adopted.
accepted.x: The Doha Conference launched the Doha Development Agenda and adopted the declaration concerning TRIPS and public health.
accepted.tq: Use the conference’s signature agenda and declaration to identify the correct option.

accepted.s: The Fifth WTO Ministerial Conference at Cancun in 2003 ended with which of the following developments?
o: It collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed.
It eliminated agricultural export subsidies.
It adopted the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS-public health declaration.
It adopted the COVID-related TRIPS waiver.
accepted.x: The Cancun Ministerial Conference collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed in that context.
accepted.tq: Avoid confusing the Cancun outcome with the outcomes of Doha and Nairobi.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth WTO Ministerial Conference at Hong Kong in 2005:
1. It included a commitment to end farm export subsidies.
2. It addressed duty-free and quota-free access for least developed countries.
3. It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Hong Kong Ministerial Conference dealt with ending farm export subsidies and duty-free, quota-free access for LDCs. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement was adopted much later at MC12 in 2022.
accepted.tq: Reject the later-outcome trap by placing each development in its conference year.

accepted.s: The WTO Ministerial Conferences held at Geneva in 2009 and 2011 were principally associated with:
o: Stock-taking
The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The formation of the G-33
The first adoption of the Singapore issues
accepted.x: MC7 in 2009 and MC8 in 2011, both held at Geneva, were primarily stock-taking conferences.
accepted.tq: Identify the common outcome of a paired conference entry.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MC9 — Bali — Trade Facilitation Agreement and interim Peace Clause on food stockholding
MC10 — Nairobi — Doha Development Agenda
MC11 — Buenos Aires — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
MC12 — Geneva — Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
accepted.x: The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 produced the Bali Package, including the Trade Facilitation Agreement and an interim Peace Clause on food stockholding.
accepted.tq: Match the conference with its characteristic package while rejecting swapped outcomes.

accepted.s: The elimination of agricultural export subsidies was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference held at:
o: Buenos Aires in 2017
Bali in 2013
Geneva in 2022
Nairobi in 2015
accepted.x: The Nairobi Ministerial Conference of 2015 adopted the outcome concerning elimination of agricultural export subsidies.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive agricultural outcome to identify the correct conference.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Eleventh WTO Ministerial Conference held at Buenos Aires in 2017?
o: It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and the COVID TRIPS waiver.
It extended the e-commerce moratorium to March 2026.
It produced no ministerial declaration and included a fisheries work programme.
It adopted a ministerial declaration and a permanent solution on public stockholding.
accepted.x: MC11 at Buenos Aires produced no ministerial declaration but included work on fisheries.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an absence of declaration from formal agreements at later conferences.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Twelfth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Geneva in June 2022:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
2. A COVID-related TRIPS waiver was adopted.
3. The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was permanently abolished.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: MC12 adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and a COVID-related TRIPS waiver. The e-commerce moratorium was extended, not permanently abolished, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false later-development statement by separating extension from abolition.

accepted.s: At the Thirteenth WTO Ministerial Conference in Abu Dhabi in 2024, which of the following was the relevant outcome concerning the e-commerce moratorium and public stockholding?
o: The moratorium was extended to 31 March 2026, while no solution was reached on public stockholding.
The moratorium lapsed immediately and a permanent public-stockholding solution was adopted.
The moratorium was extended to 2030 and fisheries negotiations were concluded.
Both the moratorium and public-stockholding issue were permanently settled.
accepted.x: MC13 extended the e-commerce moratorium to 31 March 2026 but did not produce a solution on public stockholding.
accepted.tq: Compare two simultaneous outcomes instead of treating the conference as wholly successful or unsuccessful.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fourteenth WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in March 2026:
1. It produced only a draft ‘Yaounde package’ and no ministerial declaration.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.
3. Sixty-six members signed a separate E-Commerce Agreement barring duties on digital trade.
4. A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
accepted.x: MC14 produced no ministerial declaration, the e-commerce moratorium lapsed, and 66 members signed a separate agreement barring duties on digital trade. The permanent public-stockholding solution remained deadlocked, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Check each conference outcome separately and reject the over-claim of a settlement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following developments was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in 2026?
o: India blocked the addition of the Investment Facilitation for Development plurilateral agreement to Annex 4.
India proposed making the e-commerce moratorium permanent without opposition.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched.
The fisheries Phase 2 negotiations were concluded.
accepted.x: At MC14, India blocked addition of the IFD plurilateral agreement to Annex 4, although it had the backing of 129 of 166 members. Fisheries Phase 2 was deferred.
accepted.tq: Identify the relevant negotiating position while rejecting outcomes belonging to earlier conferences.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade is correct?
o: It was created by the Doha Ministerial Conference in 2001.
It ceased to have any relevance after the establishment of the WTO.
It was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948 with 23 countries.
It was signed in 1948 and came into force in 1995 with 166 countries.
accepted.x: GATT was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948 with 23 countries. GATT continues as part of the WTO agreements even after 1995.
accepted.tq: Separate the founding history of GATT from the later establishment of WTO.

accepted.s: The Uruguay Round of multilateral trade negotiations is correctly described as the:
o: Sixth round, held from 1973 to 1979 with 23 contracting parties
Seventh round, held from 1980 to 1985 with 92 contracting parties
Eighth round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993 with 123 contracting parties
Ninth round, launched at Marrakesh in 1994 with 166 contracting parties
accepted.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993, with 123 contracting parties.
accepted.tq: Verify round number, dates, venue and participation together.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the stated aims or areas of the Uruguay Round?
o: Opening of services trade
Reduction of farm subsidies
Coverage of investment and intellectual property rights
Establishment of a worldwide common currency
accepted.x: The Uruguay Round aimed to reduce farm subsidies, open services and cover investment and intellectual property rights. Establishment of a common currency was not its aim.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the unrelated policy objective from a list of negotiation aims.

accepted.s: The Dunkel Draft consisted principally of:
o: A schedule of tariff concessions adopted at Nairobi in 2015
Proposals by Arthur Dunkel for the Uruguay Round multilateral trade agreements
A declaration on fisheries subsidies adopted at Geneva in 2022
A treaty establishing the International Monetary Fund
accepted.x: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals made by Arthur Dunkel, the GATT Director-General and Chair of the Trade Negotiations Committee, for the Uruguay Round agreements.
accepted.tq: Link a named document with its author and negotiation context.

accepted.s: The Marrakesh Agreement of April 1994 resulted in which of the following?
o: Launch of the Doha Development Agenda in 2001
Creation of the WTO on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT system while retaining GATT as part of the WTO agreements
Creation of GATT in 1947 with 23 founding countries
Adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in 2022
accepted.x: The Marrakesh Agreement created the WTO, which began functioning on 1 January 1995. GATT continued as part of the WTO agreements rather than disappearing entirely.
accepted.tq: Distinguish institutional replacement from complete legal disappearance.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the World Trade Organization?
o: Headquarters — Geneva; Director-General — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
Headquarters — New York; Director-General — Arthur Dunkel
Headquarters — Washington, D.C.; Director-General — Pascal Lamy
Headquarters — Paris; Director-General — Roberto Azevêdo
accepted.x: The WTO headquarters is in Geneva and its Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its headquarters and current head without swapping officials.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s status in relation to GATT and the WTO is correctly stated as follows:
o: India was a founding member of GATT but joined the WTO only after the Doha Round.
India was a founding member of GATT and became a founding member of the WTO.
India was not a member of GATT but became a founding member of the WTO.
India joined GATT after 1995 but was a founding member of the WTO.
accepted.x: India was a founding member of both GATT and the WTO.
accepted.tq: Test membership in both predecessor and successor institutions together.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The WTO is commonly described as the third pillar of the world economy along with:
o: The IMF and the World Bank
The ADB and the OECD
UNESCO and UNCTAD
The ILO and WHO
accepted.x: The WTO is described as the third pillar of the world economy, alongside the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard institutional trio.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A country grants an advantage in customs treatment to one WTO trading partner. Under the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, it must generally:
o: Apply the advantage only to domestic producers
Extend the same advantage to other WTO trading partners
Extend the advantage only to countries with which it has a customs union
Withdraw the advantage from all trading partners
accepted.x: MFN requires non-discrimination among trading partners, so an advantage granted to one partner should generally be extended to other WTO trading partners, subject to permitted exceptions.
accepted.tq: Apply the non-discrimination principle to a trade-policy situation.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which situation best illustrates the national-treatment principle under WTO rules?
o: A country gives an export subsidy to domestic firms.
A country grants the same tariff concession to every foreign trading partner.
An imported product, after entering the domestic market, is treated like a similar domestic product for internal taxation and regulation.
A country imposes a quantitative restriction on all imports.
accepted.x: National treatment requires imported goods to be treated like domestic goods once they have entered the market, particularly in internal taxation and regulation. Equal treatment among foreign trading partners is the MFN principle.
accepted.tq: Separate national treatment from MFN by focusing on the point after importation.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the WTO Global Trade Outlook of April 2025, India ranked what position in merchandise exports and had what share?
o: 10th position and 3.5 per cent
18th position and 1.8 per cent
15th position and 2.4 per cent
25th position and 1.0 per cent
accepted.x: India was ranked 18th in merchandise exports with a 1.8 per cent share according to the cited WTO Global Trade Outlook data.
accepted.tq: Match the rank and percentage as a single statistical pair.
accepted.sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]
